Subject: Inference node egress + service discovery: architecture review & test window

Team —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached is a first-pass network sketch (egress-flow-annotated.png) and a small example of the service-discovery config we were thinking of (service-discovery-sample.yaml). High level ask: we need to validate that our on-prem inference nodes can reach Redwood control-plane telemetry and auth endpoints while remaining within Acme's egress allowlist and our DMZ/Audit requirements.

Key questions we want to lock down before the staging window:
- Which FQNs/IPs must be reachable from the inference nodes? (we prefer hostnames + fixed IPs for allowlisting)
- Do nodes require inbound reachability from Redwood, or is the design entirely node-initiated outbound over mTLS?
- Port ranges and whether ephemeral callbacks (high ports) are required for streaming or callback hooks.
- Recommended pattern for service discovery: DNS resolution to LB vs. static config persisted on node and how to rotate when you roll control plane.

Constraints from our side:
- Outbound only through a centralized egress proxy that performs TLS inspection and allowlisting (no direct internet egress from the node VLAN).
- Strict deny-by-default ACLs on the edge firewall.
- All secrets are stored in our KMS; we need guidance on key exchange and whether Redwood supports wrapping keys with a customer KMS.

Can you confirm those details and whether the attachments cover what you need for a staging exercise? We are aiming for a 2-hour test window on Tue 21 Jul (13:00-15:00 UTC).

Attachments: egress-flow-annotated.png (diagram), service-discovery-sample.yaml (text)

Thanks,
Maya Patel

From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Inference node egress + service discovery: architecture review & test window

Maya —

Appreciate the clear diagram and sample config. Quick answers inline; see below for recommended allowlist and test checklist.

On FQNs/IPs:
- Minimum outbound endpoints (all mTLS): control.redwood.ai, telemetry.redwood.ai, oauth.redwood.ai. We publish a JSON with stable IP ranges for each environment; we'll share the staging range by EOD.
- We prefer node-initiated outbound connections only (no public inbound). All interactions are via mTLS client auth initiated by the node.

On ports and callbacks:
- Primary: 443 (HTTPS/mTLS) for control and telemetry.
- Streaming: still over 443 via HTTP/2 with long-lived connections; no ephemeral high-port callbacks required by default. If you enable advanced callback hooks (webhooks to customer endpoints) those are node->external as well, not inbound.

Service discovery:
- Option A: DNS resolution to a Redwood regional LB (recommended). Nodes resolve control.redwood.ai and use SNI to get region-specific endpoints. Works well with your egress proxy since it can apply allowlist by destination IPs.
- Option B: Static pinned config (service-discovery-sample.yaml) if you need airgap-like determinism during a release. If you choose B, ensure you have an automated rotation step for rollouts (we can provide a small agent that fetches new pins during maintenance).

KMS / Key exchange:
- We support customer-managed KMS for encrypting model keys and ephemeral secrets; integration requires a KMS endpoint reachable from control plane (we'll provide a short runbook).

Staging checklist (what we'll bring):
- Staging IP ranges and TLS fingerprints for control/telemetry (shared today).
- A lightweight agent binary to run in your staging VLAN that exercises model pulls, cache warm, and streaming token emission.
- Monitoring hooks (trace IDs) so you can map traffic through your egress proxy.

Can you confirm your egress proxy can allow outbound to the published IP set and permit long-lived HTTP/2 connections? If so we can lock the Tue 21 Jul 13:00-15:00 UTC slot and I'll send the staging IPs + test plan.

On rotation/fallback: we have a local degraded mode that lets the node serve from cached KV entries for short periods (minutes) if control plane is unreachable; it logs locally and resumes when connectivity returns. We'll document behavior for your ops team.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Inference node egress + service discovery: architecture review & test window

Maya / Alex —

Two quick clarifications from infra/runtime perspective:
- We assume an overlay network (Calico/Cilium) on the nodes. That is fine; the node outbound sockets originate from the node IPs in that overlay. If your egress proxy performs source-IP filtering, please include the overlay CIDR in allowlist or NAT those flows to your DMZ egress NAT IPs.
- For streaming and token-level telemetry we do not open extra ports. We rely on persistent HTTP/2. If you have deep TLS-inspection middleboxes that terminate TLS and re‑encrypt, we need the re‑encrypted certificate to include the Redwood CN or allow SNI passthrough; otherwise our mTLS trust will fail.

Also: if you intend to use customer KMS for wrapping secrets, we'll need a short-lived token exchange endpoint reachable from the control plane; confirm whether that endpoint is behind your egress proxy or is public.

Thanks — I'll be on the call for the test on Tue.

— Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

I've attached an updated diagram (egress-flow-annotated.png) with NAT IPs and the staging timeframe. Security (Sofia) copied to validate our KMS approach; Sofia, we plan to expose a short-lived KMS token exchange endpoint inside our DMZ on a private VIP reachable from Redwood staging control plane. Can you confirm that pattern is acceptable?

We're set for Tue 21 Jul 13:00-15:00 UTC. Please send the staging IP set and the agent binary as discussed.
